schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The door to the open-question lane: a decision Akien has to make is a QUESTION bound to the ticket (or intention) that needs it, written to `CairnCommons/questions/open-<12hex>.json` through the artifact door (verbs `question` and `answer`), standing in his operator inbox until answered; the answer IS the decision and is recorded verbatim on the question. `open_question(ticket, question, why_it_blocks, born_of=)` opens one (a question ends with '?'; a born_of must exist). `answer(qid, words, follow_ups=[...])` resolves it, records the caller class the artifact door measured (cc when CC records his chat words, akien when he answers from his own shell), and opens each follow-up `born_of` it on the same ticket — the loop goes around until the ticket has every answer. `open_for(ticket)` is what the BUILDME entry gate reads: `build_inspector.buildme_has_no_open_questions` reds while any unresolved question cites the ticket, and `transitions.inspect_entry` refuses the TICKETME→BUILDME crossing on that red. CLI: `cairn question open|answer|list|show`.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: on 2026-09-14 Akien asked 'why are we still doing rulings? we replaced that with questions that would show up in my inbox.' Measured that day: rulings had never been retired in the record — CLAUDE.md, six skills, the Stop hook and CC's own memory all said `cairn ruling open`, five packets had been opened since 2026-09-08 — while the questions lane (ruled 2026-08-01, edges-become-open-questions) existed, was read by the inbox, and had been empty since 2026-08-27. The replacement lived in his head; this tool is its translation. His design, verbatim: 'what was the ruling should now be part of the ticketing or intention recording process. slash sorted should lead to questions, and if i can't answer then right then, for whatever reason, they become open questions in the inbox. and yes, the answer to the question is the decision... ASSUMING THE ANSWER DOES NOT LEAD TO YET MORE QUESTIONS. If the answer does, we keep going around until you have all the answers you need.' And: 'we want to squeeze out the decisions toward the front of the process.' WHY A QUESTION AND NOT A PACKET: a ruling was a standalone artifact CC drafted and he confirmed — the decision lived apart from the work that needed it, and CC drafted the binary. A question is bound to the ticket by id, opened where the gap is found (/sorted), and his words are the whole record; there is nothing to draft. WHY THE GATE IS THE EXIT CONDITION: 'until you have all the answers you need' is prose until a crossing refuses; the BUILDME gate makes it physics, and the ticket that built it (9adc6fddf185) was the first measured by it — its own four questions had to be answered before it crossed. WHY BOTH CALLER CLASSES: his answer to open-690330e1cfa6 — 'yes it can come via chat. and you can also say are you sure? ... those are all fine' — the class is journaled either way, never used to refuse. WHY decisions/ STAYS: his answer to open-68aabd7eb2e0 ('yeah') — read-only record, citable by path, no migration; `cairn ruling open` refuses from now on and points here.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.question import question as Q; Q.open_question(ticket, q, why, born_of=None); Q.answer(qid, words, follow_ups=[...]); Q.open_for(ticket)`. CLI: `cairn question open --ticket <id> "<q>" --why "<what it blocks>" [--born-of <qid>]`, `cairn question answer <qid> "<his words>" [--follow-up "<q>" ...]`, `cairn question list [<ticket>]`, `cairn question show <qid>`. The inbox renders every unresolved question with its ticket and text (`cairn operator_inbox`, QUESTIONS section). Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_question.py`. Scratch world: `CAIRN_QUESTIONS_DIR` or the `root=` kwarg.
entry: Written 2026-09-14 under ticket 9adc6fddf185 (idea 2026-09-14-why-are-we-still-doing-rulings-we; intent berth intent-20260914T110302-5cac1c85f228; sorted berth sorted-20260914T110400-d54062eb0231). Patterns cited, not grafted: the record shape is the open lane's existing schema (CairnCommons/questions/_charter+why.json) with answer fields added; the write rides the artifact door as every record does; the gate lane is the same `_sieve_lane` shape as buildme_rides_the_intent and buildme_rides_the_sorted.
state_and_history: The questions are the COMMONS' records (jurisdiction: questions/*.json), journaled by the artifact door and committed with the commons. This tool keeps no state.json or history.json beside its code; the ticket's voyage is its history.
filed_edges: (a) A QUESTION RAISED AT /intent HAS NO TICKET ID YET. It binds to the intent berth path until /sorted casts the ticket; nothing yet rebinds it, so a question bound to a berth path is invisible to the ticket's BUILDME gate. OPEN — the gate reads `ticket == id` only.

(b) THE GATE READS ONE DIRECTORY. A question filed anywhere but CairnCommons/questions/ (or CAIRN_QUESTIONS_DIR) is not a question to the gate. One spelling, by design; a second store would be the drift.

(c) 'ANSWERED' IS A FIELD, NOT A JUDGEMENT. An answer of 'are you sure?' resolves the question as written; if that answer bears more questions, CC must open them as follow-ups — the tool cannot tell a decision from a deflection. His answer to open-690330e1cfa6 says both shapes are fine.

(d) THE HISTORICAL RULINGS ARE NOT REBOUND. decisions/ stays read-only and citable by path; sieves that accept 'a ruling in the same act' now also accept an answered question id, but no ruling was rewritten as a question (his answer to open-68aabd7eb2e0).
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_question.py (open through the door and the inbox shows it; answer resolves, journals the caller class, follow-ups born_of; the BUILDME crossing refused with an open question and passing once answered — with the gate reverted the crossing goes through, the hollow tooth; `cairn ruling open` non-zero; the Stop hook gone; zero skills say open a ruling; the two inspector sieves accept an answered question id). Build gate — `buildme_has_no_open_questions` at the emit chokepoint. Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) `cairn question open --ticket <id> "<q>"` does not write open-<qid>.json through the artifact door, or the operator inbox does not list it under that ticket; (2) `cairn question answer` does not resolve the question, journal the caller class, or open each follow-up born_of it; (3) a TICKETME ticket with one unresolved question crosses to BUILDME through the emit chokepoint, or a ticket whose questions are all answered is refused — and with the gate reverted the crossing must go through (the hollow tooth); (4) `cairn ruling open` exits zero, `ruling --hook` stands in the Stop hooks, or any skill tells CC to open a ruling; (5) constraint_enforcement_holds or every_exemption_cites_a_ruling_or_an_impossibility refuses an answered question id as same-act evidence, or accepts a cite of neither. WRONG INTENT: a decision arrives that no ticket or intention can bind — then standalone decisions were a real class and decisions/ reopens as an intake.
proof: proofs/test_question.py — PROVES['9adc6fddf185'] one tooth per falsifier clause; sealed under the tester. probes/no_crossing_with_an_open_question.py — the WATCHME probe: counts BUILDME crossings after the gate exists against the open-question count at each, and every answer's caller class.
owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Its users: the /sorted and /intent skills (the openers), CC recording Akien's chat answers, Akien from his own shell, the operator inbox (reader), the frontier projector cairn/tools/edges (reader), the BUILDME entry gate (reader). The records are the commons' and are gated by the artifact door. CC writes the code and proofs; Akien answers.
traces_to: Law 1 (every answered question becomes structure — the answer rides the ticket that needed it, never re-derived)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — 'until you have all the answers' is a crossing gate, not discipline)
Law 6 (a tool has users; the records are the commons')
Law 9 (his head says what SHOULD BE — the question is how the build asks it, and the answer outranks every artifact)
decisions/2026-08-01-edges-become-open-questions (the lane this tool is the second tenant of)
provenance: Born 2026-09-14 from Akien's question 'why are we still doing rulings?'. The first thing done was to exercise the shape before the tool existed: the ticket's own four spec questions were opened as open-*.json through the artifact door, showed in his inbox, and were answered in chat and recorded verbatim — then the door, the gate and the retirement were built.
learns: Nothing of its own. The lane's throughput is what the WATCHME probe measures (crossings vs open-question count, follow-up depth, caller class per answer) for the counting learning block (5a4ec289bf15) to read who answers what.
how_it_learns: It does not; a question store has no parameters to adjust. The probe beside it (probes/no_crossing_with_an_open_question.py) reports the lane's throughput on each crossing and each answer; what learns from the report is the counting learning block, not this tool.
